# Review frontend features and scenes

Apply Jason’s feature-first frontend rules with explicit composition and earned sharing.

[All skills](index.md) · [Collection overview](../../README.md) · [Research and inspiration](../../standards/framework-evidence.md)

## When to use it

Use when designing or reviewing a frontend against this chosen model.

Example request:

> Review these feature and scene boundaries without changing the framework or underlying frontend rules.

Expected result: A targeted recommendation preserving feature ownership, public surfaces and scene composition.

## A concrete example

This invented example illustrates the guidance. It is not an observed product result or a benchmark.

**Source facts and constraints:** Checkout owns its workflow state. The shared button is a UI primitive, and scenes compose features.

The before text may obscure or overstate those facts. The revision must follow the supplied facts and constraints.

**Before**

> The shared button should own the checkout workflow state.

**After**

> Keep checkout workflow state in its feature. Let the scene compose the feature with shared UI primitives.

Preserve the source facts, governing meanings and consequential constraints when applying the example to real work.

## Install and use

Install this skill from the versioned collection in a supported Agent Skills environment:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/tree/v1.6.0 --skill frontend-slice-architecture
```

Select the intended agent and installation scope when prompted. This CLI installation is separate from ChatGPT plugin registration and mobile availability. Client discovery and activation require their own verification.
